correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge1\), the transformed exponential maximum \(W_n=n\min_i e^{-X_i}\) has density \((1-w/n)^{n-1}\) on \((0,n)\). Its beta integral gives \(\mathbb E e^{-tZ_n}=n^{t+1}B(t+1,n)\), while \(\mathbb E Z_n=H_n-\log n\) and \(h(Z_n)=1+\mathbb E Z_n-1/n\). Minimizing the full two-parameter Gumbel likelihood first over location gives scalar objective \(F_n(t)\), with \(F_n'(t)=H_n-1/t-\sum_{j=1}^n(t+j)^{-1}\) and \(F_n''(t)=t^{-2}+\sum_{j=1}^n(t+j)^{-2}>0\). The derivative is negative at \(t=1\) and positive at infinity, so the global scale and location optimum is unique. The case \(n=1\) yields the golden-ratio root; comparing consecutive derivatives proves strict decrease of optimal inverse scales. A mean-value argument implies \(n(t_n-1)\to6/\pi^2\), and second-order Taylor expansion of \(F_n\) about one yields \(n^2K_n\to1/2-3/\pi^2\). Checked orientation and infinite-KL reverse support, parameter boundaries, and exact normalization. Independent direct quadrature and moment computations corroborate finite examples, not the all-\(n\) theorem.

value.rationale: The motivating information-theoretic extreme-value literature studies convergence and raises the question of relative-entropy approximation quality and rate. This population fit determines the exact best Gumbel scale and location for the maximum of any positive integer sample of exponentials, shows the finite-sample optimum scale differs systematically from its limit, and quantifies a strict leading-constant improvement from \(1/2\) to \(1/2-3/\pi^2\) over the best location-only fit. The all-size exact optimization has natural finite-sample extreme-value calibration use and is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a claim about a general domain of attraction. No statistical estimator or broad convergence theorem is asserted.
